chunks: And Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi narrated from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who forgot to perform the visitation of the House until morning, so he said: 'There is no harm in that. I myself sometimes delay it until the days of Tashreeq have passed. However, he must not approach women or use perfume.'

key_terms.أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ: The days of Tashreeq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.النِّسَاءَ: Women (in the context of marital relations)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to delay the visitation of the Kaaba after Eid al-Adha?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the permissibility of delaying Tawaf al-Ziyara until after the Days of Tashreeq, offering a practical concession for pilgrims managing post-sacrifice crowds or rituals. The specific condition of abstaining from intimacy and perfume highlights the state of ritual purity and focus required during the sacred period, reflecting the juristic emphasis on maintaining the sanctity of the Hajj rites even when extending the duration of stay.
